scope: Accept S1-LL17-a at its reviewed generated binding-vector and symbol-access scope.
exclusions: v_many is compiled but absent from the original execution corpus; Claude independently executed it. Add a retained execution case in the next derivative.

Unbinding currently uses the growing lookup. Capacity cannot shrink and failed growth pushes no binding, so it cannot allocate today; use a non-growing lookup in the next runtime derivative to make this invariant explicit.
SETF of SYMBOL-VALUE and the first-class SYMBOL-VALUE function are outside this source subset and refuse at compile time; idiomatic SETF support remains future work.

Owner-installed D1 symbols with immutable nonnegative binding indices. Index zero has global value only; dynamic binding requires a positive index. Reads/SET beyond the vector fall back to the global cell without allocation. NIL/T and registered keyword constants are protected. Package installation and assigning a new symbol index remain LL09.

TCR binding-vector element pointer/capacity is a raw interior root; scan all live element values except immediate markers. Saved binding symbol and old value remain in rooted binding records; unbinding recomputes the current slot from symbol/index. The source never stores a TLB slot address in a binding record.

Old heap vectors become unreachable after publication and must be reclaimed by LL18's collector. They are not reused by this bump-allocation implementation. Initial bootstrap vector storage remains owner-managed. The test collector copies the complete vector at legal GC-service entries and poisons the abandoned vector; it does not implement general heap collection.

A real Node Worker blocks in Atomics.wait at an entry-observation host import while compiled special bindings and roots stay live. The supervisor independently reads the shared state and resumes it. No host re-entry, JSPI or general foreign callback is claimed.

Owner-capacity exhaustion is checked refusal code 3, malformed owner metadata code 11; no engine trap or partial publication. General allocator retry/collection and recoverable heap exhaustion remain LL18.
